name: zucchini polenta fritters
instructions:
Zucchini polenta fritters — grated salted-and-squeezed zucchini folded into a cooked polenta base with parmesan, pan-fried into crisp fritters. From Adriana Rose (Quick & Easy Dishes). Replaces the old corn-fried-zucchini-slices recipe (masa-crusted rounds — see notes).

MAKES ~fritters for 4; 30 minutes total (15 prep, 15 cook).

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 2 medium zucchinis, grated (about 2 cups)
- 1 tsp salt
- 1 cup cornmeal (polenta)
- 2 cups water
- 1/2 cup grated parmesan cheese
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour
- 2 large eggs
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- 1/4 tsp garlic powder
- 1/4 tsp onion powder
- 1/4 cup chopped fresh parsley (optional)
- vegetable oil for frying

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. SALT + SQUEEZE THE ZUCCHINI: place the grated zucchini in a colander, sprinkle with the salt, and let sit ~15 minutes to draw out moisture. Then SQUEEZE out as much liquid as possible — this is what makes the fritters crispy.
2. COOK THE POLENTA: bring the 2 cups of water to a boil in a medium saucepan. Slowly whisk in the cornmeal, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce to low and cook ~5 minutes, stirring frequently, until thickened. Remove from heat and cool slightly.
3. COMBINE: in a large bowl, mix the cooked polenta, squeezed zucchini, parmesan, flour, eggs, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and parsley (if using) until well combined. The mixture should be thick but manageable — a little extra flour if it feels too wet.
4. FRY: heat ~1/4 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat (a drop of the mixture should sizzle). Drop spoonfuls in, flattening slightly with the back of the spoon. Fry ~3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Don't overcrowd — fry in batches.
5. DRAIN on paper towels. Serve warm with a dipping sauce or a dollop of yogurt.
notes:
=== SOURCE ===

Adriana Rose, Quick & Easy Dishes ('Zucchini Polenta Fritters'). Transcribed; UNATTEMPTED so far.

=== HER TIPS ===

- Squeeze the zucchini hard — moisture is the enemy of crisp.
- Oil temperature discipline: too hot burns them, too cool makes them soggy.
- Fry in batches; don't overcrowd.
- Rest on paper towels to shed oil.

=== HER VARIATIONS ===

- SPICY: 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes in the mixture.
- CHEESE SWAP: feta or goat cheese instead of parmesan.
- HERB-INFUSED: fresh basil or dill mixed in.
- GLUTEN-FREE: almond flour or GF blend instead of the AP flour.
- VEGGIE BOOST: grated carrots or bell peppers folded in.

MAKE-AHEAD: mixture keeps in the fridge up to 24 hours — fry fresh. FREEZES after frying (cool, freeze flat, bag); reheat in the oven for a crispy finish.

=== REPLACED — CORN-FRIED ZUCCHINI SLICES (SEPTEMBER 2026) ===

This file used to be corn-fried-zucchini-slices: thin mandolined zucchini rounds double-dredged (milk-egg wash, then masa harina) and high-heat pan-fried. Key lessons from that era, kept for reference: masa harina beats cornmeal for a dredge crust (finer, adheres better); iron skillets were wrong for batch-frying dredged slices (masa residue burns between batches).
